brief_data.deck: Corgi, the San Francisco AI-native insurance carrier for start-ups, closed a $106M Series B1 at a $2.6B valuation on 28 May 2026, three weeks after a $160M Series B at $1.3B. It named sports as a next vertical the same day: a brand about to be built in public.

risks.label: YOUNG BOOK
risks.detail: Corgi is two years old and its valuation runs far ahead of its premium base; a multi-year fee could look reckless to investors.
risks.counter: Pay part of the fee in cover, tie the balance to premium milestones, keep year one at Austin scale.

risks.label: REGULATED SPEND
risks.detail: A carrier's capital is watched by regulators and rating agencies; sponsorship can read as surplus leaving the balance sheet.
risks.counter: Fund it from the growth capital just raised, with the sports vertical as the stated commercial purpose.

gridfit.label: PRIME LANE
gridfit.detail: greenfield entry — partner roster being built from zero

gridfit.label: OPEN
gridfit.detail: no rival in this category lane

gridfit.label: OPEN
gridfit.detail: no rival in this category lane

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Nico Laqua before the British GP to confirm Corgi's licensed footprint for a team account, size an Official Insurance Partner entry against Cadillac's 2027 roster, and agree an Austin announcement window.

value.text: A first-year team carries general liability, cyber and technology-and-AI liability exposure from the day it opens its US entities, signs suppliers and starts generating car data. Corgi underwrites exactly those lines in-house and quotes with models rather than weeks of manual review. Within its licensed footprint it can insure the team's US operations, and the account becomes the first reference for the sports vertical it has just announced.
value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)

value.text: Corgi's customer base is founders and their investors, the guest list a new American team wants in its Austin and Las Vegas suites. A partner that pays partly in cover also lowers the team's own operating cost.
value.label: Commercial lift for the team

value.text: A joint series on what it takes to insure a start-up F1 team, told through the people standing up Fishers and Charlotte, serves Corgi's sales into sports and Cadillac's story of an American operation being built from scratch. The corgi mascot on an F1 car is the kind of asset both brands' social channels will use.
value.label: Content and ecosystem

value.text: Official Insurance Partner designation, commercial-insurance exclusivity, sidepod or halo placement, hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, driver and engineering access for Corgi's channels, and a case study Corgi can take to every league and club it pitches.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 28 May 2026 Corgi announced a $106M Series B1 led by TCV at a $2.6B valuation, three weeks after the same investor led a $160M Series B at $1.3B on 6 May. Total funding is $378M. Both figures come from the company's own releases; the founder's statement that Corgi was profitable last month is reported by TechCrunch and not audited.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: Corgi came out of stealth in January 2026 with $108M and has since doubled its valuation twice. Companies that re-price this fast spend the following quarter telling the story to customers, recruits and the next round of investors, and Corgi already invests in brand: a mascot, a named office cafe, a consumer-grade identity in a category that has none.
why_now.label: A brand about to be built in public

why_now.text: The 28 May release names trucking, small business and sports as the next verticals. A Formula 1 partnership is the fastest way to make the sports line credible to leagues, clubs and venues, and to put Corgi in front of the sports-industry buyers who sit in the paddock.
why_now.label: Sports named as a vertical

why_now.text: The British GP at Silverstone on 3-5 July falls inside the six-to-ten-week window; the United States GP in Austin on 23-25 October and the Las Vegas GP on 19-21 November are the US stages left in 2026. Teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter, so a deal agreed over the summer can be announced in Austin and run in full from 2027.
why_now.label: Calendar window

why_team.text: Cadillac's inaugural roster carries TWG AI, IFS, Core Scientific, Tenneco, Claro, Jim Beam, Tommy Hilfiger, Pirelli and Alpinestars, with no insurer and no financial-services brand. Official Insurance Partner is a clean category at a founding-partner price on a team still building its 2027 line-up.
why_team.label: The open lane

why_team.text: Dan Towriss, chief executive of TWG Motorsports and the Cadillac programme, also runs Group 1001, a US insurance and financial-services group. He can judge an AI-native carrier on its underwriting, not on its logo, which shortens the sale and raises the chance the team actually uses the product.
why_team.label: A buyer who understands the product

why_team.text: Cadillac is the grid's first-year entrant, building a 450,000 sq ft base in Fishers, Indiana while racing from Silverstone. Its exposures are those of a fast-growing company, and its story, a new American operation standing itself up in public, is Corgi's own customer story.
why_team.label: A start-up team for a start-up insurer

why_team.text: Corgi's customers are US start-ups and its buyers are US founders. Cadillac gives them Austin and Las Vegas hospitality on an American team, which is the audience match that Haas, with an insurer already on the car, cannot offer.
why_team.label: American brand, American stages

ruled_out.reason: Orion180, a homeowners insurer, has held a multi-year partnership since October 2024; the insurance lane is taken.
Aon, the insurance broker, is on the roster.
Visa and Cash App own the financial lane at title level.

ruled_out.team: Audi Revolut F1 Team · BWT Alpine F1 Team
ruled_out.reason: Revolut is title partner at Audi; Mobilize Financial Services sits at Alpine; both financial-services lanes are occupied.

ruled_out.team: Atlassian Williams Racing · Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
ruled_out.reason: Williams carries Stephens, Nuveen, Barclays, BNY and Kraken; Mercedes carries UBS, Nasdaq and Nu; crowded financial rosters where an insurer would be one logo among many.

ruled_out.team: Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team · McLaren Mastercard F1 Team · Oracle Red Bull Racing
ruled_out.reason: Coinbase, Circle and CoinPayments at Aston Martin; Mastercard title and Goldman Sachs at McLaren; Visa, Carlyle and Gate.io at Red Bull. Open on insurance but no American start-up story and no insurance-literate buyer.

brief_data.bottom_line: Two rounds in three weeks, a $2.6B valuation and a named push into sports put Corgi at the moment a brand gets built in public. Cadillac's inaugural roster carries no insurer, its chief executive runs one, and the British GP and Austin sit inside the window.

score_cells.note: Two rounds in three weeks; British GP and Austin inside the window.
score_cells.label: TIMING

score_cells.note: $378M raised at $2.6B; profitability reported, book still young.
score_cells.label: CAPACITY

score_cells.note: Playful consumer-grade brand, but sells to start-ups, not fans.
score_cells.label: BRAND FIT

score_cells.note: Sports vertical named; 2027 rosters close in Q4.

score_cells.note: MODE A: liability and cyber cover a first-year team needs.

brief_data.the_case_p1: Corgi announced on 28 May a $106M Series B1 led by TCV at a $2.6B valuation, three weeks after the same investor led its $160M Series B at $1.3B on 6 May. Total funding stands at $378M for a company founded in 2024 that came out of stealth in January with $108M at a reported $630M. Founder-CEO Nico Laqua told TechCrunch the company was profitable last month and will expand from start-ups into trucking, small business and sports. It writes general liability, cyber and tech-and-AI liability as a full-stack carrier, not a broker.
brief_data.the_case_p2: Insurance is on the grid, but thinly. Orion180, a Florida homeowners insurer, has been on the Haas car since October 2024; Aon is at Ferrari as a broker. Fintech is crowded: Visa and Cash App at Racing Bulls, Revolut at Audi, Mobilize Financial Services at Alpine. Cadillac, the grid's new American entrant, carries none of it, and the executive who runs the team also runs an insurance group.

brief_data.value_content: MODE A - operational. A first-year team stands up US entities, a factory, supplier contracts and a growing data estate, with general liability, cyber and tech-and-AI liability exposure from day one. Corgi underwrites those lines in-house with models that quote in minutes, so it can cover the team's US operations, within its licensed footprint, and make the account its first sports reference. Cadillac gains a partner that pays partly in cover and brings founders to Austin.
brief_data.why_team_para: Cadillac's inaugural roster is TWG AI, IFS, Core Scientific, Tenneco, Claro, Jim Beam, Tommy Hilfiger, Pirelli and Alpinestars: no insurer and no financial-services brand. Its chief executive, Dan Towriss, also runs Group 1001, a US insurance and financial-services group, so an AI-native carrier is a product he can judge. The team is building a 450,000 sq ft base in Fishers, Indiana while racing from Silverstone; Corgi's start-up customers and Cadillac's American story meet at Austin.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Insurance Partner of the Cadillac F1 Team. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, with an option to start at Austin in 2026. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in underwritten cover. Scope: commercial-insurance exclusivity, sidepod or halo placement, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality for founder customers, a content series on insuring a start-up team.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  Two rounds in three weeks doubled the valuation by 28 May, and brand budgets are set in the quarter after a raise. The British GP (3-5 July) falls inside the window, and the United States GP in Austin (23-25 October) is the natural announcement stage.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Laqua co-founded Corgi in 2024 and holds the CEO and CTO titles; the brand, the mascot and the all-night office cafe are his. Path: Emily Yuan, Co-Founder and COO. No chief marketing officer or CFO is listed on any source checked.
brief_data.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the sports vertical he named.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Nico, you named sports as Corgi's next vertical the day you hit $2.6B. Cadillac is a start-up team with no insurer on the car, run by a man who runs an insurance group. 25 minutes before Silverstone to see the numbers?”
